summary.name: Google Compute Engine
summary.one_liner: Google Cloud's infrastructure-as-a-service for creating and running virtual machines, including GPU and TPU instances for AI/ML workloads.
keywords: run a server in the cloud
host a website on a vm
use_cases: Hosting web and app servers on cloud VMs
Training or fine-tuning large language models on GPUs or TPUs
Running batch jobs at a discount with Spot VMs
Migrating on-premises servers to the cloud
Running containers directly on VMs or with Google Kubernetes Engine
Backing up VMs and persistent disks
summary.what_it_does: Compute Engine lets you create and run virtual machines on Google's infrastructure with predefined or custom machine types (custom up to 96 vCPUs, up to 8 GB memory per core). Machine families cover general purpose, compute, memory, storage, GPU, TPU-accelerated, and bare metal workloads. Block storage options include Persistent Disk and Local SSD. The page also describes pricing discounts (Spot VMs, committed use, sustained use), live migration on host failure, managed instance groups for autoscaling, and an MCP server so AI agents can provision and resize VMs.
notable: Free tier includes one e2-micro VM per month, plus $300 in new-customer trial credits
Spot VMs can cut costs by up to 91% for fault-tolerant jobs
Offers GPUs and Cloud TPUs for AI/ML training and inference
Live migration moves VMs to another host in the same zone when hardware fails
caveats: Paid beyond the free tier; pricing varies by machine type, storage and network usage
Some machine families (such as Z3H Bare Metal and GA/M4N) are listed as preview
Windows Server 2008 R2 and 2012 R2 images are listed among supported OS options; newer Windows versions are not named on the page
